soc2/data-retention-secure-disposal.applicability_reason: The plugin writes derived markdown and JSON into tracked repository paths such as knowledge-base/, compliance-base/catalog/, CLAUDE.md and docs/, which persist and need defined retention and disposal.

ranked.rationale: The only retention question this product raises is how long derived knowledge-base and compliance-base artefacts stay in the developer's repository, which a per-dataset schedule can record.
Session transcripts and derived files exist solely on developer workstations, so media wipe at machine decommissioning is the one physical disposal path that genuinely applies.
Cryptographic erasure needs per-record keys over an encrypted store, and this plugin encrypts nothing and owns no store to shred.
There is no object storage in this product; outputs are committed files whose deletion is a git operation, not a lifecycle-expiry rule.

soc2/data-subject-rights-complaint-handl.applicability_reason: There are no user accounts and no personal data is collected, stored or processed as a product function, so there is no data subject whose information could be accessed, corrected or deleted.

options: OpenBao (Transit secrets engine + PKCS#11 HSM auto-unseal)
soc2/encryption-cryptographic-key-manage.applicability_reason: The plugin reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from the environment and makes an outbound call to the Anthropic API carrying repository text, so transmission and key handling must be protected.

ranked.component: OpenBao (Transit secrets engine + PKCS#11 HSM auto-unseal)
ranked.rationale: The only key material in play is the developer's own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OAuth token, so a lifecycle store is the nearest fit if issuance of those ever needs managing rather than leaving them in the environment.
Application-layer encryption would only matter if the plugin held data of its own at rest, and it deliberately adds no store beyond files the developer already controls.
There is no listening service and no Kubernetes here; the single outbound call to the Anthropic API gets its transport security from the client library, not from certificates we issue.

options: Cloud provider compliance attestations (AWS Artifact / Google Cloud compliance reports / Azure Service Trust Portal)
soc2/environmental-safeguards-facility-m.applicability_reason: There is no hosting facility or data centre in scope; the only execution environment is the developer's own machine, which they own and control.

soc2/external-communication-incident-rep.applicability_reason: Engineers who install the plugin from GitHub need a channel to report vulnerabilities and to be told of changes affecting security.

ranked.rationale: A static, self-published security contact costs no infrastructure and fits a project distributed as a public GitHub repository with nothing hosted.
Reports about this product will be vulnerabilities in its Python hooks and skills, and it gives those a place to land and be triaged.
Complaint intake presumes customers, and the product states its only user is the engineer who installed it in their own checkout.
A status page communicates availability of a running service, and this plugin has no hosted component that can be up or down.

soc2/identity-access-management.applicability_reason: Although the product has no login, access to the GitHub source and releases and handling of the developer's API credentials still require identity and access controls.

ranked.rationale: The product has no login layer of its own, so its only application is issuing operator identities for the self-hosted governance tools the authors run.
Joiner-mover-leaver provisioning needs a user population and downstream directories to sync, and this product explicitly has no accounts, sessions, roles or permissions to provision into.

soc2/incident-response-recovery.applicability_reason: A defect or compromise in a plugin that reads session transcripts and writes into developers' repositories must be triaged, contained, communicated and reviewed.

ranked.rationale: A realistic incident here is a released hook corrupting tracked files in a developer's own repository, which needs declaration, timeline and root-cause review far more than it needs detection tooling.
It could announce a bad release to developers who installed the plugin, though GitHub release notes and the marketplace manifest already reach that audience.
Alert routing needs a monitored system emitting signals, and this product runs as short-lived local processes with nothing paging anyone.

options: OWASP Coraza WAF (+ OWASP Core Rule Set)
soc2/infrastructure-network-boundary-end.applicability_reason: The plugin is distributed as executable code that runs on developer machines and makes an outbound API call, so malicious-software and endpoint controls remain relevant.

ranked.rationale: Developer workstations are the only machines this product touches, and host-level detection with file-integrity monitoring over the tracked paths it writes is the one applicable protection layer.
Syscall-level observation could watch the local Python processes the hooks spawn, but it is built for servers and containers this product never runs on.
The product's whole network boundary is one outbound call to the Anthropic API, which egress policy could in principle pin, but there is no cluster for it to enforce in.

ranked.component: OWASP Coraza WAF (+ OWASP Core Rule Set)
ranked.rationale: A web application firewall protects inbound HTTP traffic, and this product has no network service listening and no perimeter to defend.

soc2/personal-data-quality-management.applicability_reason: No personal data is collected, stored or processed as a product function, so there is no stored personal information whose accuracy could be maintained.

soc2/physical-access-control-secure-medi.applicability_reason: No facility, data centre, hardware or storage media is operated for this product; everything runs on and is stored on the developer's own machine under their control.

soc2/privacy-breach-detection-notificati.applicability_reason: No personal information is collected, stored or transferred by the plugin, so there is no personal information that could be subject to unauthorized use or disclosure.

soc2/privacy-notice-consent-lawful-colle.applicability_reason: The plugin collects no personal information at all and has no sign-up or account, so there is no collection event at which notice or consent could be required.

soc2/processing-integrity-validation-pip.capability: Processing integrity: validation, pipeline & output verification
soc2/processing-integrity-validation-pip.applicability_reason: The product's core function is a pipeline that distils session transcripts and catalogs into derived documents and gates PRD/plan writes, so inputs and outputs must be validated and verified.

ranked.rationale: The plugin's output is derived markdown and JSON such as the constraint catalog, and declarative checks in the same Python runtime can verify those artefacts before they are written into the developer's repository.
Hook invocations are short synchronous runs on a laptop, so durable execution would add a server the product otherwise does not need to guarantee steps that already complete in one process.
Inputs and outputs are files committed to the developer's own git repository, which already provides the tamper-evident history WORM storage would supply.
There is no streaming intake or authorized external source feeding this plugin; it reads a local transcript file, so schema-validated topics and dead-letter queues have nothing to carry.

soc2/risk-assessment-fraud-risk-governan.applicability_reason: Risks to the plugin's objectives, including compromise of code shipped into developers' repositories, must be identified, analysed and responded to.

ranked.rationale: A small register with scoring and review cycles is sized to a project whose risk surface is one plugin, one repository and one outbound API dependency.
It brings fuller SOC 2 mapping and treatment workflow, which is more machinery than a developer tool with no hosted service and no customer data needs to carry.
Management-override and journal-entry analytics require transactional records, and this product processes no financial or user data of any kind.

soc2/system-monitoring-alerting-audit-lo.capability: System monitoring, alerting & audit log retention
soc2/system-monitoring-alerting-audit-lo.applicability_reason: The hooks act on the developer's repository and call an external API, so their activity needs integrity-protected logging to support post-hoc investigation.

ranked.rationale: File-integrity monitoring on the developer machine covers the one thing worth watching here — unexpected changes to the tracked paths the hooks write into the repository.
Hook runs do produce discrete log output that could be aggregated, though on a single developer workstation there is little volume to index.
Metric scraping needs a long-running process to scrape, and this plugin exists only for the duration of a hook invocation.
It requires cloud infrastructure this product explicitly does not run, and its proprietary licence is the only non-OSS entry in this pool, so it is ranked last for the licence gate to decide.

soc2/vendor-third-party-risk-management.applicability_reason: The Anthropic API is a fixed recipient of prompt content and GitHub and Claude Code are relied on for distribution and execution, so third-party risk must be assessed and monitored.

ranked.rationale: The recipient set is fixed by the code to a single vendor, the Anthropic API called with the developer's own credentials, so a compact register with recurring assessment covers it without extra machinery.
A full vendor lifecycle platform with contractual obligation tracking and offboarding workflow is oversized when there are no subprocessors and no per-deployment variation in recipients.
Continuous external exposure scanning targets vendor internet-facing assets that this project neither operates nor is contractually positioned to probe.

soc2/vulnerability-management-remediatio.applicability_reason: The plugin is Python code with dependencies that is installed into developers' repositories, so it must be scanned and remediated for known vulnerabilities.

ranked.rationale: The plugin's real exposure is known CVEs in its Python 3.12 dependencies, which dependency scanning in the repository's own CI addresses directly.
Filesystem and configuration scanning of the same repository adds coverage of the shipped skill and manifest files without needing images or a cluster.
Aggregation and SLA tracking is useful but heavy for the small finding volume a single-repository plugin generates, where GitHub issues already hold the work.
Cloud posture scanning has no target here because the product runs on developer machines with no infrastructure or cloud account of ours to assess.
